subject: [AMBER] Error: an illegal memory access was encountered launching kernel kNLSkinTest

messages.author: Christian Seitz
messages.body:
Hello,
I have run a short minimization on a system, and am trying to run the
heating for it. When I do this, I get this error before any cycles are
finished:
Error: an illegal memory access was encountered launching kernel kNLSkinTest
My heating input file looks like this:
Heat
&cntrl
imin=0,
ntx=1,
irest=0,
nstlim=500000,
dt=0.002,
ntf=2,
ntc=2,
tempi=10.0,
temp0=300.0,
ntpr=1000,
ntwx=1000,
cut=8.0,
ntb=1,
ntp=0,
ntt=3,
gamma_ln=5.0,
nmropt=1,
ig=-1,
restraint_wt=1.0,
restraintmask='.CA,C,O,N&!:WAT'
/
&wt type='TEMP0', istep1=0, istep2=2000000, value1=10.0, value2=300.0 /
&wt type='TEMP0', istep1=2000001, istep2=5000000, value1=300.0,
value2=300.0 /
&wt type='END' /
I have seen this error when using amber 18, amber 20 and amber 22. I have
also seen it for the ff14sb and ff19sb force fields. I do not have any
ligands present in my system, which appeared to be the culprit for someone
previously (
http://archive.ambermd.org/202011/0195.html
), though I do have
dozens of bicarbonate ions that I have added to my solvent. Additionally,
my restraint weight is not too high as was also seen previously (
http://archive.ambermd.org/202110/0250.html
). What might be the issue?
Thanks in advance!
Best,
Christian

messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Tue, Aug 23, 2022, Christian Seitz via AMBER wrote:
>
>I have run a short minimization on a system, and am trying to run the
>heating for it. When I do this, I get this error before any cycles are
>finished:
>
>Error: an illegal memory access was encountered launching kernel kNLSkinTest
What is the box size in your system?  Also, the following:
1. use the checkstructure action in cpptraj to make sure you don't have any
bad bonds or contacts.
2. Run a short simulation on the CPU, with ntpr=1.  Make sure the starting
energy is very close to the final energy from minimization.  Look for
any problems that might arise.
....good luck...dac

which doesn't go away on minimizaiton.  Use the checkstructure action in
cpptraj to look at bond lengths.
....dac

messages.author: Christian Seitz
messages.body:
Hi David,
I don't see any bad bonds using the default parameters of check:
bic = loadpdb bicarbonate_amber.pdb
check bic
prot = loadpdb protein.pdb
check prot
Checking parameters for unit 'bic'.
Checking for bond parameters.
Checking for angle parameters.
check:  Warnings: 1
Unit is OK.
Checking parameters for unit 'prot'.
Checking for bond parameters.
Checking for angle parameters.
check:  Warnings: 1
Unit is OK.
When I tried to use checkstructure, I got syntax errors. If checkstructure
is still supported, it does not contain the same syntax as check does, even
though the documentation would indicate that they are identical:
https://amber-md.github.io/cpptraj/CPPTRAJ.xhtml#index-check
The warnings for my protein and bicarbonate ion are just that they are not
at a charge of exactly 0.
Best,
Christian

messages.author: Daniel Roe
messages.body:
On Thu, Sep 1, 2022 at 12:00 PM Christian Seitz via AMBER
<amber.ambermd.org> wrote:
> When I tried to use checkstructure, I got syntax errors. If checkstructure
> is still supported, it does not contain the same syntax as check does, even
'checkstructure' is a CPPTRAJ command. Were you trying to use it in
CPPTRAJ or LEaP? If you were trying to use it in CPPTRAJ and got an
error, please post the exact error message(s) as well as the exact
input you used.
-Dan
